title: Virginia SCC GS-5 Large-Load Rate Decision — Phase 65 Northern Virginia large-load delivery review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Northern Virginia large-load delivery reporting pack. The Virginia SCC approved Dominion Energy Virginia's GS-5 class for future customers at or above 25 MW, with a January 1, 2027 effective date and minimum billing provisions intended to allocate large-load investment risk.
key_findings: The decision creates a separate rate class for customers with demand of at least 25 MW.
The SCC described minimum billing commitments of 85 percent for distribution and transmission and 60 percent for generation.
The regulatory decision and future effective date precede customer contracts, facilities, energization, billing, and reliability outcomes.
why_it_matters: Which records connect load forecasts, local land-use rules, utility decisions, transmission, environmental permits, water, service acceptance, and reliability? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. The record makes customer commitment and cost allocation explicit conversion gates alongside physical power capacity.
ftfn_relevance: Adds a finance-and-risk layer to the compute-corridor stack.
Separates an approved tariff from customer-specific service.
Creates a later trail for implementation, realized load, cost, and reliability.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
The decision does not establish that any named customer has signed under GS-5.
It does not prove transmission, generation, or distribution capacity is available.
The future rate design is not evidence of realized bills, load, reliability, or project economics.
